title: The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse
subject: English

notes.heading: Theme
notes.text: The story highlights childhood innocence, a shared love for freedom, and how a deep-seated pride in family values, honor, and integrity can guide wayward youth to make the right moral choice.

summary: "The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse" by William Saroyan is a heartwarming story about two poor Armenian boys, Aram and Mourad, who belong to the Garoghlanian tribe, a family renowned for its integrity and honesty for over eleven centuries. The narrative begins on a summer morning when nine-year-old Aram is awakened by his thirteen-year-old cousin Mourad, who is notorious for inheriting the "crazy streak" of the tribe, much like their eccentric Uncle Khosrove. Aram is astonished to see Mourad sitting on a magnificent, beautiful white horse. Though Aram desperately longs to ride, he struggles to reconcile the sight with their extreme poverty, knowing that his family cannot afford such an animal and that stealing it would violate their tribe's sacred code of absolute honesty. Rationalizing that stealing a horse for a ride was not the same as stealing it for money, Aram joins Mourad for an exhilarating ride through the countryside. While Mourad rides with instinctive grace and control, showing a natural understanding with animals, Aram is thrown off when he attempts to ride alone. The boys hide the horse in a deserted vineyard belonging to a farmer named Fetvajian and continue their secret early morning rides for two weeks. The plot thickens when the true owner of the horse, a lonely Assyrian farmer named John Byro, visits Aram's house and mentions the theft of his white horse. A few days later, the boys encounter John Byro while walking the horse to its hiding place. Byro examines the horse thoroughly, noting that its teeth match his stolen animal perfectly, but because of the legendary honesty of the Garoghlanian family, he refuses to believe the boys stole it, concluding instead that the horse must be the twin of his own. Touched by Byro's profound faith and trust, the boys experience a quiet awakening of conscience. The very next morning, they stealthily return the horse to John Byro's barn, where the dogs surprisingly remain quiet because of Mourad's gentle handling. Later that afternoon, a joyful John Byro visits Aram's mother to show them his returned horse, noting that it has grown stronger and better-tempered, proving that trust and honor can gently guide wayward youth back to their core values.

qa.q: You will probably agree that this story does not have a breathless adventure. Then what is the reason for the special appeal of the story?
qa.a: The story is appealing because of its simple and humorous narration, lovable characters and interesting situations. The innocence of Aram and Mourad makes the story enjoyable. It also shows the importance of honesty, family values and the desire to enjoy freedom.

qa.q: Did the boys return the horse because they were conscience-stricken or because they were afraid?
qa.a: The boys returned the horse mainly because they realised that keeping it was wrong. They belonged to the Garoghlanian family, which was famous for its honesty. Their conscience reminded them of their family values, so they finally returned the horse.

qa.q: “One day back there in the good old days when I was nine and the world was full of every imaginable kind of magnificence...” The story begins in a vein of nostalgia. Can you narrate some incidents from your childhood that you remember vividly?
qa.a: This is a personal-response question. One may write about a memorable childhood experience such as playing with friends, visiting grandparents or going on a school trip. Such memories remain special because childhood is a time of innocence, happiness and freedom.

qa.q: The story revolves around the character of Mourad. Comment on his character.
qa.a: Mourad is adventurous, lively and freedom-loving. He has a strong imagination and loves animals. Although he takes the horse without permission, he is not truly dishonest. He eventually returns it because he understands the importance of his family’s reputation for honesty.
